newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. truck destroyed in Bosnian revenge blast.
newsitem.headline: U.N. truck destroyed in Bosnian revenge blast.

text.p: A United Nations truck was destroyed in two explosions overnight in Bosnian Serb-controlled territory, the lastest attack in retaliation for a NATO crackdown on suspected war criminals, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday.
No one was injured in the explosions which occurred after midnight in the eastern town of Bratunac in the country's Serb republic, spokesman Alex Ivanko said.
"Two explosions in Bratunac resulted in the demolition of a U.N. vehicle," Ivanko told Reuters.
U.N. officials believe rocket-propelled grenades were used in the attack and one unexploded grenade was found at the scene, he said.
The pick-up truck was parked outside the apartment of an international police monitor. A Western official who asked not to be named said the monitor was a U.S. citizen.
Since NATO pounced on two Serbs indicted for war crimes earlier this month, international agencies and peacekeeping soldiers have been targeted by a low-level retaliation campaign in Serb territory.

Small-scale explosions have damaged vehicles and apartments of monitors working for the international police and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which is supervising local elections in Bosnia.
Western officials say the campaign has been orchestrated by Serb hardliners, loyal to wartime leader Radovan Karadzic, who feel threatened by the tougher NATO policy towards suspected war criminals.

No one has been injured so far in the attacks which appear designed to discourage NATO from launching more arrest operations against suspects, including Karadzic, who have been indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Netherlands.
British soldiers seized and extradited one suspect and shot dead another who resisted arrest in the Prijedor region two weeks ago.
